title: Omni-Life: Benchmarking Omnimodal Real-Time AI Assistants in People's Daily Lives
abstract: arXiv:2611.02835v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Real-time omnimodal assistants are expected to support people in everyday life, but audiovisual understanding alone does not establish whether they can provide timely and appropriate help. We introduce Omni-Life, a benchmark grounded in real-world user needs, deployment scenarios, and device-dependent observations. It combines controlled video synthesis for hazardous situations and edge cases with annotated real-world videos under a shared temporal protocol. The benchmark contains 400 videos: 290 requiring assistance, with 555 required intervention events, and 110 requiring silence throughout to test whether models can withhold unnecessary responses when no assistance is needed. We evaluate twelve configurations featuring mainstream real-time omnimodal models, jointly assessing event coverage, response content, timing, and unwanted output. At most 4.48% of videos requiring assistance are handled completely correctly. To examine practical

translated_title: Omni-Life：面向人们日常生活的全模态实时AI助手基准测试
translated_abstract: 实时全模态助手被期望能够支持人们的日常生活，但仅有音视频理解能力并不能确定它们是否能提供及时且恰当的帮助。我们提出了Omni-Life，这是一个基于真实世界用户需求、部署场景和设备相关观测构建的基准。它将对危险情况和边缘案例的受控视频合成与经过标注的真实世界视频相结合，并遵循统一的时间协议。该基准包含400个视频：其中290个需要助手提供帮助，包含555个需要干预的事件；110个全程需要保持沉默，用以测试模型在无需帮助时能否克制不必要的回应。我们评估了十二种主流实时全模态模型配置，联合考察事件覆盖率、回应内容、回应时机以及多余输出。结果显示，在需要帮助的视频中，最多仅有4.48%被完全正确地处理。为了检验实际（应用表现），（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出基于真实用户需求的Omni-Life基准来评估实时全模态AI助手在日常生活中的表现，发现现有主流模型最多只能完全正确处理4.48%需要帮助的情境。
en_tdlr: Omni-Life, a benchmark grounded in real-world user needs for evaluating real-time omnimodal AI assistants in daily life, reveals that mainstream models can fully and correctly handle at most 4.48% of videos requiring assistance.
